name: Pressure dressing scar therapy

card.summary: Sustained compression garments or dressings worn over healing skin to flatten raised scars and make them less visible.
card.aka: Pressure garment therapy, compression therapy for scars
card.note: Garments are usually fitted through burn or scar clinics; effectiveness is described as unclear in some reviews.

quick.overview:
Pressure dressing scar therapy uses snug garments or dressings that apply steady pressure over a healing wound. The goal is a flatter, softer, paler scar, which is a visible appearance outcome after burns, surgery or deep cuts.

It is described as the standard treatment for raised (hypertrophic) scars after burn injury. Clinical reviews describe its effectiveness as unclear, and research continues into how to measure the pressure garments actually deliver.
quick.how: Custom-fitted elastic garments are typically worn for much of the day and night during scar maturation, which can take many months, and are often used alongside massage or silicone products. A clinic usually measures and fits them.
quick.risks: Poorly fitting garments can cause discomfort, skin irritation or blistering, and wearing them for long periods in warm weather is a common complaint. Fitting by a burn or scar clinic is typical.

lead: Pressure dressing scar therapy is the application of continuous pressure, through elastic garments, bandages or pressure dressings, to a healing wound with the aim of reducing raised scarring and improving how the scar looks [1][2]. It is used most often after burns, where hypertrophic scars (raised, red, thick scars confined to the wound) are common [1][2].

A 2021 study in the journal Burns describes pressure garment therapy as the current standard treatment for hypertrophic scars following burn injury, and reports on a new portable device designed to measure the pressure actually delivered at the scar surface [1]. Wikipedia notes that pressure or massage is generally applied to early scars in the first months, and that the effectiveness of garments is unclear [2].

chain: Scar tissue lies flatter and softer while it matures
angle.text: People with burn or surgical scars wear fitted garments to keep a healing scar flat as it matures. The intended payoff is a scar that stands out less in texture and colour.

infobox: Early in scar maturation, over months [2]

paras: Hypertrophic scars arise when excess collagen builds up in a healing wound, producing a raised scar that can itch or hurt and usually fades over one to two years. Mechanical tension on the wound is considered a leading cause [2]. Pressure therapy is intended to counter this, and is applied from early in healing, with silicone sheeting and other options used later if needed [2].

A practical problem for clinicians is knowing how much pressure a garment delivers. A 2021 study compared a novel portable pressure-measuring device based on silicon piezoresistive sensors with the PicoPress manometric sensor, which is regarded as a highly accurate reference, using in vitro measurements at the scar-garment interface [1].

The 2021 study above evaluated a measurement device in vitro rather than patient outcomes [1]. Wikipedia's summary of the literature states that pressure garments are commonly used to prevent hypertrophic scarring after burns, and that evidence of how well they work is unclear [2].

refs.title: Comparison between the portable pressure measuring device and PicoPress for garment pressure measurement on hypertrophic burn scar during compression therapy
